A_target.statement:
Let $f: P \to Q$ and $g: Q \to P$ be monotone maps between [[Definition:Ordered Set|ordered sets]] with $\map f x \le y \iff x \le \map g y$.
Then $g$ preserves all [[Definition:Infimum of Set|infima]] that exist in $Q$, and $f$ preserves all [[Definition:Supremum of Set|suprema]] that exist in $P$.

B_source.statement: [[Definition:Right Adjoint|Right adjoints]] preserve all limits, and left adjoints preserve all colimits.

substitutions.categories: ordered sets, with a morphism x -> y exactly when x <= y

object_map.reformulation: Regard ordered sets as thin categories, in which adjunctions are Galois connections and limits are meets.

validity_conditions: In a thin category every diagram commutes, so a limit of a family is just its infimum.
For a mapping, preimage is both a left and a right adjoint, so it preserves unions and intersections, while direct image preserves only unions.
proof_plan: View $P$ and $Q$ as categories with a unique morphism $x \to y$ when $x \le y$; monotone maps are functors.
The hom-set bijection $\map {\operatorname {Hom} } {\map f x, y} \cong \map {\operatorname {Hom} } {x, \map g y}$ says exactly $\map f x \le y \iff x \le \map g y$, so $f \dashv g$.
In such a category, the limit of a family is its infimum and the colimit is its supremum.

By the source result, $g$ preserves infima and $f$ preserves suprema.
{{qed}}
